name_reason: Follows convention data_fd2_<domain=ui>_<descriptor>; descriptor reflects the data type (template array of menu slot token IDs). No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix matching its own/any data address). Consistent with sibling templates in uitab.c (data_fd2_ui_field_command_menu_options_template, data_fd2_ui_inline_action_menu_template, data_fd2_ui_save_load_newgame_menu_template). Name accurately describes purpose and type.
purpose: Base text-token IDs for the 4-slot game options (settings) menu: BGM / SE / Speed / Other.
logic_summary: const int32[4] = { 0x12, 0x14, 0x16, 0x18 }. Sole reader fd2_game_options_menu_loop (@ 0x1728c; data load @ 0x172a5, read @ 0x172aa) REP-MOVSDs all 4 dwords into a local menu_slot_0..3 buffer (MOV ECX,4; ESI=this array; REP MOVSD -> 32-bit elements), then for each slot adds 0 or 1 according to the current toggle state to select the ON/OFF (or Slow/Fast) label variant: slot0 = 0x12 + (bgm_enabled==0); slot1 = 0x14 + (sfx_enabled==0); slot2 = 0x16 + (game_speed!=0); slot3 = 0x18 + (terrain_hud_enabled==0). Source array is never written; only the stack copies are mutated. Paired with data_fd2_ui_game_options_menu_state_template @ 0x53F02 (per-option enable/disable flags).
element_semantics: Each int32 is the base (ON / Slow) text-token ID for one game-options menu slot: [0]=0x12 BGM, [1]=0x14 SE, [2]=0x16 Speed, [3]=0x18 Other. The reader adds 0 or 1 to each per the live toggle state to pick the ON/OFF (or Slow/Fast) label variant.
notes: Ghidra PLATE was null; created a concise data plate via run_script_inline PLATE_COMMENT (content consistent with the src comment, src as authority). src comment block (uitab.c lines 24-35) was already accurate, precise and conclusion-style -> comment_verdict=keep, uitab.c NOT edited (only the shard is staged for this symbol). Const confirmed by Ghidra: WRITES=0 across all 4 dwords of the array (only 2 READs + 1 DATA pointer-load, all from fd2_game_options_menu_loop). save_program returned 'Unable to lock due to active transaction' (a concurrent Ghidra driver holds the transaction lock); the plate write itself was applied and verified via read-back, and the user keeps their own .gpr backups, so program save is deferred to the lock owner / session end per project Ghidra rules.
